configs.description: Fixed 1+1 120 W AC supply, dual feed, 100 to 240 V. NO GEOMETRY CHANGES HERE and that is deliberate: no held document shows the AC faceplate, so where its two inlets sit and what replaces the RTN legends is unknown. See the ac-feed-faceplate gap
configs.name: ac

configs.description: Fixed 1+1 120 W DC supply, dual feed, -36 to -75 V on the two three-post screw terminal blocks the faceplate carries. This is the build every held elevation and photograph shows, and the one the drawing is measured from
configs.name: dc

gaps.note: HIG section 8 tables the four system lamps (SYNC, STAT, PSU, PWR) and the management jack, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The Port Overview draws an up/down green pair in the web of every SFP and SFP+ column, so which port each lamp belongs to is clear from the arrows; what its colours and behaviours mean is not. Every port lamp therefore keeps common/led-dot's off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Nine rows of the system-lamp tables are annotated 'need NOS to activate this feature', so these may be NOS-defined rather than merely undocumented - a different fix, and the reason this is vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: Both held elevations and all three photographs show the DC build: two three-post screw terminal blocks under RTN / -36 - -75V legends. The datasheet offers a '120W AC PSU, fixed dual feed' and the HIG has an AC Version PSU Overview section, but its figure is a close-up of the inlet rather than a faceplate elevation, so where the two AC inlets sit on the 440 mm face and what replaces the terminal legends is not established. The ac configuration therefore changes no geometry and says so; it is not a skin of the dc one.
gaps.wanted: an AC-version front elevation, or a photograph of the AC faceplate

gaps.note: The two fixed supply feeds are real, distinguishable things - the HIG's PSU lamp table tells PSU1-good-PSU2-bad apart from PSU1-bad-PSU2-good - but they are not addressable in this manifest. A fixed supply seats nothing, so there is no bay; the six screw terminal posts are panel metal and are drawn as decor; and the library has no terminal block component to place over them. The PSU lamp therefore points at the chassis and the PSU 0 / PSU 1 legends are chassis silkscreen, which loses the per-feed link a consumer would want. Recorded rather than papered over with a group nothing joins.
gaps.wanted: a terminal-block or power-inlet component that a fixed feed can be placed as

gaps.note: The four system lamps measure about 4.1 x 2.5 mm on a 2.47 mm centre pitch and the library's nearest part, common/led-rect@1, is 4.6 x 2.6 - taller than the pitch allows. Placed on their measured pitch the four parts overlap by 0.13 mm each, which L13 is right to reject, so the column is stretched to a 2.62 mm pitch and is 0.6 mm taller than the vendor prints it.
gaps.wanted: a ~4.1 x 2.5 mm indicator component, or a caliper on the lamp window

gaps.note: The stacked optical rows measure a 15.8 mm belly-to-belly pitch here - 14.05 to 29.85 in the front photograph, 14.7 to 30.7 in the guide figure once its vertical error is removed - where std/sfp-ganged's own contract records 15.00 mm measured from a TE 2007562-6 cage and the sibling S9500-22XST's photograph gave 15.0. Row pitch is not governed by any spec, so a vendor is free to differ and this may simply be a different cage; but two of this library's devices now carry two different numbers for the same nominal assembly and neither has been checked against hardware.
gaps.wanted: a caliper on the cage, or a vendor mechanical drawing of the faceplate

gaps.note: Five screws are visible along the lower edge of the rear photograph on roughly a 100 mm pitch and are drawn there, but no figure dimensions them and the photograph resolves 0.27 mm per pixel only in x - its vertical is compressed by the drop shadow. The six grilles either side of them ARE measured; the fasteners are not.

No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name only S9502-16SMT, and with a fixed supply and no fans there are no FRU ordering lines either, so this device has no part number of any kind in the intake. Per the S9510-28DC precedent in this library, whose SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no PDF, orderable SKUs for the AC and DC builds exist somewhere.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs

attrs.note: datasheet - Physical, Performance, Environmental, Regulatory Compliance, Timing and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim and semicolon-separated, untidied, including the SANS 2332 / SANS 2335 and NRCS entries that mark this as a South-Africa-approved variant of the family.

cage-mirroring.note: The stacked SFP and SFP+ rows are drawn UNMIRRORED, which is what the same render-against-photograph test established on the S9500-22XST: rotating a std/sfp-ganged moves its drawn cavity 1.13 mm, so a mirrored pair reads a cavity pitch of 12.7 or 17.3 mm against 15.8 unmirrored. This device's own front photograph gives 15.4-15.8. Stated as a measurement of this device rather than inherited from the sibling, though the sibling is where the technique came from.

chassis.note: datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 1RU, 440 x 250 x 43.5 mm', weight 4.32 kg; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple (17.32" x 9.84" x 1.71") and the same weight, and Figure 5 dimensions the depth twice - 250 mm for the chassis and 264 mm over the 14 mm the front terminal covers project. 440 is the body: the HIG ships a separate 50.4 x 43 x 20 mm rack mount bracket as accessory 3, so the 19 inch mounting hardware is additional to 440 and is not drawn. The HIG's weight row is headed 'Chassis without FRU' and this chassis HAS no FRU - the supply is fixed and there are no fans - so for this device that heading names the whole shipping unit.

connector-shells.note: Every bright metal strip on this faceplate is PANEL and is drawn in panel.decor, not as part of a component: std/rj45-ganged and std/sfp-ganged draw the aperture and stop at it, and a dark aperture on a dark faceplate is invisible. Five shells are drawn - the two stacked jack blocks, the 2x2 copper block and the two optical blocks - each sized from the placements it sits behind plus the flange the guide shows, which measures 1.1-2.7 mm and is narrower than the connector bodies behind the panel.

fanless.note: datasheet key feature, 'Fanless chassis design', and Figure 5 labels the rear elevation 'Fanless' under a bracket spanning all six grilles. There are therefore no fan bays, no fan group and no fan lamp: the STAT/SYNC/PSU/PWR row is the whole indicator set, which is why this device's lamp column is four tall where its powered siblings are five. The rear grilles are convection openings, not blanked fan positions, and nothing in the guide offers a fan kit. AIRFLOW IS A CHASSIS FACT HERE, NOT A CONFIGURATION ONE, and the first draft of this file got that wrong. It tried `airflow: convection` on both configurations, which the schema rejects because the configuration-level enum is deliberately only the two directions: a configuration's airflow answers which airflow SKU the customer ordered, and a fanless box offers no such choice. `chassis.airflow` is the field that carries the cooling scheme and it already has the right word - `passive` - so that is where it sits. The two configurations remain and differ on the thing this vendor actually sells two of, the AC and DC feed.

front-layout.note: drawing - HIG Port Overview at 8.705 px/mm, measured on the 600 dpi page render. Left to right: a full-width honeycomb band along the top; the PSU 0 and PSU 1 three-post terminal blocks with their RTN / -36 - -75V legends; the 1PPS and 10MHz SMB jacks stacked above the model wordmark; the four-lamp column with its printed legend block and the RESET pinhole below; the management RJ45 over the USB 2.0 Type-A in one silver shell; the ToD RJ45 over the console RJ45 in a second; the four 1G copper ports in a 2x2 shell; a honeycomb field; then the eight SFP and four SFP+ in two shells, the SFP+ one on a printed BLUE ground; a second honeycomb field and the earth symbol at the right edge. Shell extents measured off the light mask: management 164.74-181.28, ToD/console 186.34-202.54, RJ45 206.44-240.91, SFP 301.80-364.06, SFP+ 365.79-400.94. The terminal posts measured 4.83 mm wide on a 9.54 mm pitch, PSU 0 at 21.94/31.48/41.01 and PSU 1 at 78.12/87.66/97.19, a 56.18 mm offset between the two blocks.

front-vertical.note: photo-anchored. All three port blocks share one band. The front photograph - the best-proportioned source held, 0.4 percent out on aspect - puts the SFP apertures' dark centres at y 14.05 and 29.85 with a 5.9 mm bright web between them, and the Port Overview's drawn cells agree at 14.7 and 30.7 once its 1.4 percent vertical error is taken out. The mean of the two, 14.4 and 30.3, is what the rows are placed on: a 15.8 mm belly-to-belly pitch, wider than the 15.00 mm std/sfp-ganged records from a TE 2007562-6 cage, which is a vendor choice rather than a standard and is stated here because the two numbers will otherwise look like a mistake. The ganged shells are 34.1 mm tall, far more than the openings need, because this vendor prints the port numerals on the shell above and below the apertures rather than on bare panel. THE LAMP COLUMN IS DRAWN 0.6 mm TALLER THAN IT MEASURES: the four lamps sit on a measured 2.47 mm pitch and common/led-rect@1 is 2.6 mm tall, so four of them will not fit in the measured 9.88 mm block without overlapping. They are placed on a 2.62 mm pitch centred on the measured block instead, which closes the printed gap between neighbours to nothing. See the system-lamp-size gap.

ground-stud-size.note: the hardware installation guide lists, in its package contents, a screw kit for the grounding lug of 2 x M4*L8.0mm screws, and its grounding steps lock the grounding lug to the designated grounding location with 2 M4 screws: the `stud-size` of ground-1 and ground-2. The accessory lug is one two-hole lug held by both screws.

jack-orientation.note: read from the silhouettes at 2.4-2.6x on the 600 dpi render, using the rule that std/rj45-ganged draws the latch keyway DOWN with its contacts at the TOP. The ToD jack (upper of its pair) has the keyway UP and carries rotate: 180; the console below it does not. The management RJ45 has the keyway up and is likewise turned, with its green and amber lamps sitting on the bezel above the aperture rather than inside the jack. On the 2x2 copper block the upper row's integrated lamps are at the TOP corners and the lower row's at the BOTTOM, so the upper row is unrotated and the lower carries rotate: 180. That sense was got backwards on the S9500-22XST last night and caught only by the matched-scale render; it is applied the corrected way round here and re-checked the same way.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9502-16SMT end of life end of sale' - no announcement found; the vendor product page and the datasheet PDF are live. none-announced is a real finding here, not an absence of looking.

port-pitch.note: measured from a feature that repeats ONCE PER PORT, not from the drawn cells' centres. The guide fills each port cell as a solid block with a numeral on it, and cell-to-cell centres would give the module pitch rather than the port pitch. Here the two agree: the SFP cell edges fall at 304.7, 318.8, 332.9 and 347.2 - a 14.2 mm pitch against the SFF-8433 standard's 14.25 - and four 14.25 mm openings from 304.7 end at 361.7 against a shell measured to 364.06, so the total span checks out as well as the pitch. The SFP+ block reads the same 14.25 from its two cells (366.9 and 381.15). The RJ45 block is the exception: its 34.47 mm shell over two columns gives a 14.94 mm column pitch, wider than std/rj45-ganged's own 12.7 mm width, so those two jacks are centred in their columns rather than abutting and 2.2 mm of shell shows between them.

power.note: THE SUPPLY IS FIXED, WHICH CHANGES THE MODEL AND NOT JUST THE PROSE. The datasheet says 'Fixed, 1+1 redundant PSU' and lists '120W DC PSU, fixed dual feed' and '120W AC PSU, fixed dual feed'; the HIG's PSU Overview sections say '1+1, Fixed power supply unit (PSU)' and show no release latch, no handle and no bay. So there are no components.bays on this device at all - the two feeds are panel features, drawn as the six screw terminal posts the DC faceplate carries, and PSU 0 and PSU 1 are silkscreen over them rather than bay ids. Datasheet 'Typical power: 45.1 Watts (no transceiver)' is the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare; no maximum is published in either document, and the per-feed input ratings (AC 100-240 V 2 A, DC -36 to -75 V 4.5 A) are supply-side and are not converted into a draw figure.

rear-layout.note: photo-measured - the rear product render is the best image held of any face on this device at 3.745 px/mm, and Figure 5's rear elevation agrees with it. Six circular convection grilles, each 37.4 mm across, on a measured 50.0 mm pitch from 26.4 to 313.7 mm, with plain metal to their right. The grille diameter and their measured height agree to 0.3 mm (37.4 against 37.7), which is the check that they are circles and that the photograph's scale is sound. Their vertical centre reads 23.85 mm in the photograph against a panel mid-height of 21.75; the 2.1 mm is the photograph's top edge blur, so they are drawn centred. Five screws along the lower edge are placed on the 100 mm pitch the photograph shows, positions estimated.

sources.note: UfiSpace S9502-16SMT datasheet for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, timing, power, environment and compliance; S9502-16SMT Hardware Installation Guide (s9502-16smt-hig) for the Port Overview elevation on page 10, the Figure 5 overview drawing with its dimensions and callout list, the Component Physical Information table, the LED tables and grounding; three vendor product renders (photos/s9502-16smt-1-angle, -2-front, -3-rear) for colour, counts, and the two measurements the drawings could not settle. TWO FIGURES WERE GATED AND BOTH PASS, which is unusual for this vendor. The Port Overview measures 3830 x 384 px across the 440 x 43.5 mm face: aspect 9.974 against a true 10.115, 1.4 percent, so the horizontal is used directly at 8.705 px/mm and the vertical carries a 1.4 percent correction. The horizontal scale was validated rather than assumed: the drawn SFP cells come out on a 14.2 mm pitch against the SFF-8433 standard's 14.25, and the four-column block's total span matches four of them. Figure 5's top view measures 890 x 500 px against 440 x 250 mm - aspect 1.78 against a true 1.76, 1 percent - so the top face is measured rather than proportioned. The FRONT PHOTOGRAPH is the best-proportioned source of the three at aspect 10.16 against 10.115 (0.4 percent) and is what the vertical band is anchored to.

stack-orientation.note: Declared in stack-exceptions with the reading that keeps them otherwise: the 6 SFP pairs (port-4/port-5 to port-14/port-15).

system-lamps.note: drawing - four lamps, not five, at x 133.49 on a 2.47 mm pitch with centres at y 22.42, 24.89, 27.36 and 29.83, beside a printed white legend block at 137.28-143.26. The HIG section 8 table names them SYNC, STAT, PSU and PWR and gives each its own vocabulary, transcribed onto each lamp. The PSU row is the one worth reading twice: it distinguishes PSU1-good-PSU2-bad (solid yellow) from PSU1-bad-PSU2-good (blinking yellow), which is a per-feed distinction a colour-only model would lose. The lamps measure about 4.1 x 2.5 mm and common/led-rect@1 is 4.6 x 2.6, the closest part held.

timing-block.note: drawing - two SMB jacks in one column at x centre 124.6, 6.3 mm across the drawn hex against common/smb-jack's 7.0, on rows at y centres 8.4 and 19.5, labelled 1PPS above and 10MHZ below. The datasheet calls both input/output on one connector each - '1 x 1PPS input/output SMB', '1 x 10MHz input/output SMB' - so unlike the S9500-22XST, which splits each into an IN and an OUT jack, this device has one jack per function and the faceplate agrees. ToD is 'input/output RJ45' on a single jack in the stacked pair.

verification.note: Rendered and compared against the front and rear photographs at a matched 8 px/mm. The port band lands within 0.2 mm of the photograph on all three blocks - SFP apertures centred 14.0/29.85 against the photograph's 13.9/29.95, SFP+ 14.0/29.85 against 13.85/29.65, copper 15.65/28.2 against 15.5/27.9 - and the copper block's row-to-row cavity pitch comes out at 12.55 against 12.4 measured, which is the check that its rotations are the right way round rather than mirrored. Horizontally the shells and both optical blocks agree to better than a millimetre. ONE THING DID NOT AGREE: the six DC terminal posts read 4.83 mm wide in the guide figure and 6.1 mm in the photograph, with their centres 1.35 mm apart. The figure resolves 0.11 mm per pixel and the photograph 0.85, and every other feature measured from that same photograph agrees with the figure to 0.3 mm, so the figure's number is carried and the disagreement is written down here rather than split.

views.note: Six views. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and Figure 5, which puts the front terminal covers' 14 mm projection at the BOTTOM of its top view; the two long stadium reliefs and the five bottom-edge screws are measured off that drawing, which passes the aspect gate at 1 percent. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an estimated position. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): Figure 5's callout inset shows the grounding lug on the RIGHT side close to the FRONT face, which is where the two-hole lug is drawn and the one asymmetric feature on either side face - so the depth-axis convention is load-bearing here and not merely stated. Screw positions on both side faces are estimated.
